clue.text: Outlaw experiencing life as a bird?

parts.note: the robin is a familiar garden bird
the suffix -hood names the state of being something, as in childhood

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about a fugitive who has turned into a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, 'experiencing life as a bird' is robin-hood, the condition of being a robin, just as childhood is the condition of being a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the legendary English outlaw of Sherwood Forest.

clue.text: Popular music, something often encountered at the seaside

definitions.text: something often encountered at the seaside
definitions.meaning: ... line the shore, and seaside ... is a stick of hard candy sold at British resorts

explanation.surface: Pop music and a trip to the coast, two parts of a summer holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock is both a music genre and a hard stone, or the striped candy sold at British seaside towns.

clue.text: Woman to briefly boil eggs, at the outset

parts.note: to blanch vegetables is to plunge them briefly into boiling water

indicators.note: at the outset points to the opening letter of the word eggs

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: boil eggs briefly, first thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Blanche is a female first name, as in Blanche DuBois of A Streetcar Named Desire.

clue.text: Definitely not cancelling women's public talk

indicators.note: cancelling says the women's letter is struck out of the phrase before it

parts.note: 'in no wise' is an old phrase meaning not at all, so nowise means definitely not
W is the abbreviation for women, as on clothing sizes or toilets

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to let women's public speeches be called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cancelling' strikes W out of NOWISE.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise can mean talk or comment in public, as in making noises about a plan.

clue.text: British, in playing golf, say, mostly not going well

indicators.note: in tells us the British letter is placed inside the golfing phrase
mostly says the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: golf is played on the links, so a golfer is on the links

explanation.surface: A British golfer's round going badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims ON THE LINKS to ON THE LINK, and 'in' puts B inside. A links is a seaside golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: On the blink is an idiom for a machine that is faulty or working badly.

clue.text: Avoid love

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to dodge it
a British endearment, like love; in cricket it is also a zero, like love in tennis

explanation.definitionFit: Duck means dodge, and in northern English it is an affectionate address, much as love is.

clue.text: Silly craze recalled fairly heartlessly

indicators.note: recalled, called back, has the word for the craze read backwards

parts.note: a fad is a short-lived craze

indicators.note: heartlessly strips fairly of all its middle letters, leaving only the outer pair

explanation.surface: A daft trend remembered with only half-hearted fairness.
explanation.definitionFit: Daffy is an informal word for foolish or crazy, as in Daffy Duck.

clue.text: Day off upheld in European Parliament? That's a bloomer

indicators.note: in puts the reversed pair inside the parliament

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament, a parliament in Europe

indicators.note: upheld in a down clue means the letters are lifted to read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A holiday being supported in the EU's parliament, followed by a remark about a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upheld' makes FFOD, which 'in' places within the Irish parliament. 'European Parliament?' suggests the EU body, but the question mark allows any parliament in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A daffodil is a flower, so it is a bloomer in the sense of something that blooms, not a blunder.

clue.text: Hide bit of wood around new section of course?

parts.note: an animal's hide is its fur

indicators.note: around means the wooden piece wraps round the letter for new

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: Instructions to wrap a bit of timber in animal skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps LOG round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A furlong, an eighth of a mile, is the unit by which racecourses are marked out.

clue.text: Sure injecting drug into damaged artery is history

parts.note: yes is an affirmative, like sure

indicators.note: injecting signals the drug is put inside other letters
into names the letters that receive the drug
damaged signals that the letters of artery are rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A grim scene of a drug being injected into a damaged artery, and that being in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' makes TERYAR from ARTERY, and 'injecting ... into' puts E inside to give TERYEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesteryear means the past, time gone by, so it is history.

clue.text: Children behaving wildly in vehicle

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for children, as on admission prices
someone running riot is behaving wildly, a riot of activity

explanation.surface: Kids running amok in the back of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: Children who are 'a riot' are wild and out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a two-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle of the ancient world.

clue.text: Scoundrels accommodating remote depressive states

indicators.note: accommodating means the scoundrels hold the other word inside them

parts.note: cads are dishonourable men, scoundrels
far means distant, remote

explanation.surface: Rogues putting up with distant moods of gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' signals containment; 'remote' must be read as a plain synonym for distant, not as a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: Cafard is a French loan for melancholy or the blues, so cafards are bouts of low spirits.

clue.text: Plan that is a recurring idea, but not initially

parts.note: sc. is short for scilicet, Latin for namely or that is

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter of the word for the idea is dropped

parts.note: a theme is a motif that keeps coming back

explanation.surface: A plan described as a running idea that wasn't there at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' drops the T of THEME.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a systematic plan or programme of action.

clue.text: Wolf, evasive, returning to back of butte

parts.note: coy can mean reluctant to give details, evasive

indicators.note: returning means the little word to is read the other way
back of picks the final letter of butte

explanation.surface: A shy wolf heading back to the rear of a flat-topped hill in the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns TO into OT. A butte is an isolated steep hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The coyote is also called the prairie wolf, a wild dog of North America.

clue.text: Perhaps film-star's hot — bother getting upset about skill

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go around the word for skill
getting upset signals the letters of bother are thrown into disorder

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: A film star running hot and getting upset over craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' makes ETHROB, and 'about' wraps it round the skill. The 's is short for is, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart-throb is an attractive celebrity adored by fans, and a film star is one example.

clue.text: Senior figure in boat group's upset about failure in race

indicators.note: about says those rearranged letters surround the others
upset says the letters of groups are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken with its s, giving the letters of groups

indicators.note: a failure in the word race means it breaks down and its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A band member is distraught over a defeat in a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams: 'upset' scrambles the band word and 'failure in' jumbles the contest word, and 'about' wraps the first round the second. 'Senior figure' suggests a boss, but the role is at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A supercargo is the officer on a merchant ship who manages the cargo on behalf of its owner.

clue.text: Cumbrian river valley last to take prime position

indicators.note: says the final letter of the valley word moves up to the front

parts.note: a dene is a narrow wooded valley

explanation.surface: In a Cumbrian valley, the runner-up takes first place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to take prime position' moves the final E of DENE to the front. Cumbria is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eden is a river flowing through Cumbria to the Solway Firth.

clue.text: Offering temptation, friend embraces university lecturer bearing sign of being married

indicators.note: embraces says the friend holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter
a wedding ring shows someone is married

explanation.surface: A seductive tale of a friend hugging a married academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' signals containment; the lecturer 'bearing' the sign of marriage puts it ahead of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Alluringly means in an enticing, attractive way, which is how something tempting is offered.

clue.text: Endless complaint about one supporting account? I am surprised!

indicators.note: about says the shortened complaint goes around the other letters
Endless means the complaint word loses its final letter

parts.note: a grouse is a grumble or complaint

indicators.note: in a down clue the letter supporting another sits below it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A never-ending gripe about someone backing an account, met with astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' leaves GROUS; in a down clue 'supporting' puts the one beneath the account, and 'about' wraps the trimmed complaint round them.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Gracious!' is an exclamation of surprise, as in 'Good gracious!'.

clue.text: Staff harbouring a fugitive? That's cuckoo!

indicators.note: harbouring means the staff gives shelter to the letter inside it

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
a runner is someone on the run, a fugitive

explanation.surface: Someone hiding an escaped prisoner, with a cry that the idea is mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbouring' puts A inside ROD. 'cuckoo' looks like crazy, but it is the bird family.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadrunner is a fast-running bird of the American Southwest belonging to the cuckoo family.

clue.text: A first: corps replaced by Australian pilot

indicators.note: replaced by says one letter of the winner gives way to another

parts.note: the victor is the one who comes first
C is an abbreviation for corps

explanation.surface: A military first: a corps swapped for Australian troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced by' swaps the C of VICTOR for A, giving VIATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is someone who flies aircraft, a pilot.

clue.text: A delightful thing recalled in story

indicators.note: recalled means the phrase is called back, read in reverse order

parts.note: a gas is an informal word for something great fun

explanation.surface: A pleasant memory retold as a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns A GAS into SAGA.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story, originally an Old Norse prose narrative.

clue.text: Old style trade ruined company

indicators.note: ruined signals the letters of trade are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm brought down by old-fashioned commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' turns TRADE into ARTDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the decorative design style of the 1920s and 1930s, now a period style.

clue.text: Tense character in Macbeth making sudden movement

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense
the three witches are characters in Shakespeare's Macbeth

explanation.surface: A nervous actor in Macbeth giving a jerk on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitch is a small involuntary jerk or spasm.

clue.text: Measurements of length, the very thing adopted by Baden-Powell's groups

indicators.note: adopted by means the young scouts take the word in

parts.note: Robert Baden-Powell founded the Scout movement, whose junior groups are the Cubs
it means exactly what is wanted, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: Scout packs adopting a perfect unit of measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopted by' signals containment. Cub Scouts are the junior branch of the movement Baden-Powell founded.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubit is an ancient unit of length based on the forearm, from elbow to fingertip.

clue.text: Notes brought in to purchase rabbit

indicators.note: brought in to says the notes are placed inside the word for buying

parts.note: to buy is to purchase
N is short for note, so NN is notes

explanation.surface: Banknotes handed over to buy a rabbit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought in to' signals containment; 'Notes' are musical notes abbreviated, not banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bunny is a child's word for a rabbit.

clue.text: Hindu festival? Some time later

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Hindu festival due some time later.
explanation.definitionFit: A mela is a Hindu fair or religious gathering, such as the Kumbh Mela.

clue.text: Annoys German aboard vehicle

indicators.note: aboard means the German letter climbs inside the vehicle

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A German passenger on the bus irritates everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' puts G inside BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to irritate or pester them.

clue.text: Runs a decrepit hotel, home to vermin

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: decrepit, worn out and falling apart, signals the letters of a hotel are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone manages a run-down hotel overrun by rats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decrepit' turns HOTEL into THOLE. 'Runs' looks like a verb of management, but it is the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rathole is a hole where rats live, or by extension a squalid dwelling.

clue.text: French verse form, right-hand page with Auden's translation

parts.note: RO is short for recto, the right-hand page of a book

indicators.note: a translation turns the words into something else, so the poet's name is rearranged

parts.note: W. H. Auden, the poet, whose name supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A French poem printed on one page alongside Auden's English version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' turns AUDEN into NDEAU.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a French fixed form of poem with a refrain and only two rhymes.

clue.text: Offers to cage rook or rooks?

indicators.note: to cage means the offers enclose the letter for the chess piece

parts.note: bids are offers, as at an auction
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: Bidding to put a rook, or several, in a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cage' puts R inside BIDS. The question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooks are crows, so they are birds, an example of the category.

clue.text: A bit of sense, holding back my number, concealing identity

indicators.note: holding means the sense word contains the reversed pieces

parts.note: nous is common sense or practical intelligence

indicators.note: back means the words that follow are read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone withholding their phone number to keep their identity secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes ONYM, and 'holding' places it within the word for sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Anonymous describes someone whose name is unknown or withheld, so their identity is hidden.
